slot.brief: Three point charges fixed at corners of an equilateral triangle; find the force on one charge by vector-adding Coulomb contributions from the other two.

stem: Three identical positive charges of $2.0\ \mu\text{C}$ are fixed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side $0.30$ m. Taking $k=9.0\times10^9\ \text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-2}$, find the magnitude of the net force on one charge.

verdicts.working: Each pairwise force is $F=kq^2/a^2=0.40\,\text{N}$. The two forces meet at $60^\circ$, so the resultant is $F\sqrt{3}=0.40\sqrt{3}\,\text{N}$.

working:
$F=\dfrac{kq^2}{a^2}=\dfrac{(9.0\times10^9)(2.0\times10^{-6})^2}{(0.30)^2}=0.40\ \text{N}$
The two force vectors have angle $60^\circ$.
$F_{\text{net}}=\sqrt{F^2+F^2+2F^2\cos60^\circ}=\sqrt{3}F=0.40\sqrt{3}\ \text{N}$

Independent check: Each pairwise force is $F=kq^2/a^2=0.40\,\text{N}$. The two forces meet at $60^\circ$, so the resultant is $F\sqrt{3}=0.40\sqrt{3}\,\text{N}$.
solution:
Each of the other charges exerts a force $F=\dfrac{kq^2}{a^2}=\dfrac{(9.0\times10^9)(2.0\times10^{-6})^2}{(0.30)^2}=0.40\,\text{N}$. The two forces are separated by $60^\circ$, so
$$F_{\text{net}}=\sqrt{F^2+F^2+2F^2\cos60^\circ}=\sqrt{3}F=0.40\sqrt{3}\,\text{N}.$$
